turns.content: Two circular transiting planets orbit the same star and share an albedo and heat-redistribution convention. Derive how equilibrium temperature scales with orbital distance, taking sin(i) approximately one.

For planet mass much smaller than stellar mass, derive how the radial-velocity semiamplitude scales with planet mass and orbital distance. How does its ratio relate to Doppler shifts measured in the same spectral line?
Combine the temperature and radial-velocity scalings to express a planet's equilibrium temperature in terms of semiamplitude and planet mass, then form the Planet1-to-Planet2 ratio.
Evaluate the ratio for masses 7 and 5 Earth masses and line shifts 0.03 and 0.04 Angstrom, respectively.
Report the result as a conditional estimate, noting the unreported exact inclinations and the common heat-redistribution assumption.
Check the numerical result from the shift ratio and mass ratio and explain the main precision limits.
Give the final equilibrium-temperature ratio with its modeling qualification.
